learningObjectives: Explain the components involved in connecting Java applications to databases.
Construct a basic JDBC workflow using connections, prepared statements, and result sets.
Choose safe database interaction patterns that reduce SQL injection risks.

activities.title: JDBC Architecture
activities.instruction: Explore how a Java application communicates with a relational database.

content.concept: JDBC provides a standard Java API for interacting with relational databases. A Java application uses JDBC APIs together with a database-specific driver to establish connections and execute SQL operations.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The application containing the business logic and database operations.
The standard Java interfaces and classes used for database access.
Database-specific implementation that enables JDBC communication with the target database.
Represents an active session through which SQL operations can be executed.
The relational database storing and processing application data.

activities.title: JDBC Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a parameterized database query.

content.concept: A typical JDBC query obtains a connection, creates a PreparedStatement, supplies parameter values, executes the query, processes the ResultSet, and closes resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: PreparedStatement Builder
activities.instruction: Build a parameterized query that safely searches for a user by email.

content.concept: PreparedStatement uses placeholders such as ? for parameter values. Parameters are supplied separately from the SQL structure, which helps prevent SQL injection caused by concatenating untrusted input into SQL statements.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: ResultSet Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore how JDBC processes rows returned from a query.

content.concept: A ResultSet represents rows returned by a database query. Its cursor initially sits before the first row, and next() advances the cursor. Getter methods such as getString() and getInt() retrieve column values from the current row.
